name: Kuo 2016 IC/BPS
question: Does suburothelial onabotulinumtoxinA added to hydrodistension reduce pain more than saline injection and hydrodistension in refractory IC/BPS?

design.population: Sixty patients with IC/BPS and persistent or recurrent symptoms after at least two conventional treatments for at least 6 months, excluding Hunner lesions, included eight men and 52 women; mean age was 52.9 ± 14.3 years in the 40-patient toxin arm and 50.2 ± 13.2 years in the 20-patient saline arm.
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Outcome Measurements, p 610; Table I, p 611

verdictNote: Week-8 pain reduction favored onabotulinumtoxinA; dysuria and overall adverse events were higher at week 8.
takeaway: In 60 patients with refractory IC/BPS without Hunner lesions, suburothelial onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U plus hydrodistension reduced week-8 pain more than saline injection plus hydrodistension (mean VAS change −2.6 versus −0.9; P = 0.021).

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Kuo HC, Jiang YH, Tsai YC, et al. "Intravesical botulinum toxin-A injections reduce bladder pain of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome refractory to conventional treatment - A prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2016;35(5):609-614. doi:10.1002/nau.22760

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 8; mean difference is onabotulinumtoxinA minus saline
results.note: Mean difference of −1.7 points calculated from reported mean changes; no confidence interval reported. Table I gives baseline VAS 5.1 versus 3.7 (P = 0.056), whereas Table II gives 5.3 versus 3.7.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table II, p 611

results.measure: GRA improvement of at least one point at 3 months
results.note: Results text gives 25/40 at 3 months; the abstract instead gives 26/40 and labels it 63%. No confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Evaluation and Follow-up, p 610; Results, p 611

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 8, mL
results.note: Between-arm mean difference of 113.2 mL calculated from reported changes; no confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table II, p 611

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 8, mL
results.note: Between-arm mean difference of 67.2 mL calculated from reported changes; no confidence interval reported.

harms.label: No adverse event at week 8
harms.locator: Full text, Table III and Results, pp 611-612
harms.note: The paper reports a higher overall adverse-event incidence in the Botox group at week 8 (P = 0.033); the abstract says adverse events did not differ.

harms.label: Urinary retention at week 8
harms.locator: Full text, Table III and footnote, p 612
harms.note: The patient with retention also had a urinary tract infection.

delivery.label: Endoscopic treatment and perioperative care

values.exp: 100 U onabotulinumtoxinA in 10 mL saline; twenty 0.5 mL suburothelial injections (5 U each), posterior and lateral walls, trigone spared
values.ctl: Twenty 0.5 mL suburothelial normal saline injections at the same sites

delivery.note: Both arms had hydrodistension at 80 cm H₂O for 15 minutes, an overnight 14 Fr Foley catheter, and cephalexin 500 mg every 6 hours for 7 days.
delivery.locator: Full text, Randomization and Intravesical Injection, pp 610-611

reports.dateLocator: Full text, title-page publication data, p 609
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Evaluation and Follow-up, p 610
